title: The tavern
logline: The cedar-shake tavern in front of the garage. Its regulars. Its jukebox through the wall. The tavern is never named.

panels.composition: The tavern from the highway side, evening: cedar shake, a beer sign, three trucks, the garage's roofline visible behind. The sign above the door is drawn — and the name on it is a wood-grain blur, as if weathered off.

image.prompt: a cedar-shake roadside tavern at evening with a beer sign and three pickup trucks, a garage roofline visible behind it, the name on the sign above the door weathered into an unreadable wood-grain blur, muddy digital flats
image.notes: The tavern's name is never drawn legibly. Reserved through 2025.

panels.composition: Inside, briefly: the bar, three REGULARS on stools who have been on those stools since the mill closed, a jukebox with one Springsteen. WOOD at the end with a beer he'll nurse for an hour. BARNABY under the stool, allowed.

balloons.text: You the kid in the garage.
Huh. Thought that was a raccoon.

image.prompt: inside a dim tavern, three old regulars on bar stools, a jukebox, a young man at the end of the bar with a beer and a small dog under his stool

panels.composition: The jukebox. 8:59. A regular's hand on the button.

image.prompt: close-up of a weathered hand pressing a button on an old jukebox beside a clock reading 8:59

panels.composition: The garage, from inside, 9:00. Wood back at the table. The wavy lines through the wall. He knows every word and draws through it. The dog's ear.

image.prompt: a garage studio at night with muffled music lines coming through the wall, a young man drawing through it, a dog with one ear up, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: The tavern, named nowhere. 'Thought that was a raccoon.' The Springsteen at nine.
